Alex (Acme): Hey team — heads up: after last night's rollout (r-20261103-3 rolled to 100% at ~03:12 UTC) our downstream vendor ingestion started crashing with JSON parse errors. Only started after the rollout.

Alex (Acme): Failure seen in their consumer logs: `JSONDecodeError: Invalid \x escape at position 54` and also `Expecting value: line 1 column 10 (char 9)`. They say their parser expects `items` to be an array but the model now returns a stringified array in some cases.

Alex (Acme): Example raw response we captured from the API (redacted request_id: req_9fXc):
```
{
  "items": "[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"foo\"},{\"id\":2,\"name\":\"bar\"}]",
  "meta": {"source": "redwood-text-2-v2"}
}
```

Alex (Acme): Repro steps: 1) POST to /v1/generate with payload prompt: "serialize inventory as JSON array" + `structured_output: true`, 2) model returns `items` as a raw string with backslashes. Impact: 3 customers (paying) affected, ~18% of their ingestion calls fail, pipeline retries cause spikes in latency and billing.

Maya (CS): Sorry about that — can you paste the request_id and the exact model/route used? Also did you have `enforce_schema` or post-processing toggles enabled on your integration?

Alex (Acme): request_id=req_9fXc, model=redwood-text-2-v2, route=prod-global, we set `structured_output: true` but not `enforce_schema`. Canary was at 10% earlier today then promoted to 100%.

Jin (ML Eng): Thanks — initial hypothesis: a postprocessor change aimed at escaping unsafe chars accidentally stringified nested JSON when heuristics hit. We pushed a small serializer tweak in rollout r-20261103-3. Can you share the exact raw bytes (response body) and response headers? Need the `x-redwood-model` and `x-rollout-id` headers if present.

Alex (Acme): Pasting raw body (from their consumer without our client re-encoding):
```
{"items":"[\"{\\\"id\\\":1,\\\"name\\\":\\\"foo\\\"}\",\"{\\\"id\\\":2,\\\"name\\\":\\\"bar\\\"}\"]","meta":{"source":"redwood-text-2-v2"}}
```

Maya (CS): Got it. This shows double-escaping. We'll escalate to runtime/serving. Priya, can we consider immediate rollback of r-20261103-3 or a patch?

Priya (Prod): Deploy-bot shows rollout r-20261103-3 completed at 03:12 UTC to prod-global. I'll schedule a partial rollback to previous stable for the affected cluster and open a hotfix ticket. Rolling back to r-20261028-7 for prod-global now (estimating ~8min to propagate).

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: rollback r-20261028-7 -> prod-global. ETA 8m. Incident: #INC-20261103-17 created.

Jin (ML Eng): On the fix side: we'll revert the serializer change and add stricter unit tests for structured outputs and the `enforce_schema` path. Also adding a feature flag `stringify_nested_json` default false.

Alex (Acme): Thanks. Temporary ask from them: can we provide a blunt mitigation like `response_format=json` toggle or a header that forces raw JSON output (no escaping)? They prefer that while we fix.

Maya (CS): We'll follow up with a timeline and confirm once rollback completes. Also asking engineering for a raw dump of the response for all failing request_ids this morning.

Jin (ML Eng): Action items: 1) collect raw responses + headers for req_9fXc and siblings (assigned to Alex/CS), 2) rollback in progress (Priya), 3) hotfix patch to revert serializer change and add tests (Jin), 4) short-term client knob to enforce unescaped structured output (product/infra).

Alex (Acme): Appreciate it. I'll send any additional sample failing request_ids and hold on escalating to their legal/compliance team until we have rollback status.

Maya (CS): Noted — will update once rollback finishes and when we have hotfix ETA. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
